SMTO-LLM-0035 — Model response could not be parsed

GUID: 761b9ef3-de1d-4b74-8047-ded6c359a0d6
Slug: llm-parsing-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • Something unexpected went wrong while SMTO was getting a structured answer from the model. This message is broad, so it doesn't show which part failed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details hold the exact unexpected problem, which is the only clue to what broke.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. If the check also fails, the problem is the model connection; if it passes, it's specific to this step.
  3. If the check passes, try the work once more in a new task. A one-time glitch won't repeat, while a real fault will, which is useful to know before reporting it.

What success looks like

  • The new task's step completes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who installed or manages SMTO. Don't raise the output limit or other model settings hoping it helps; nothing shows this error comes from them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • structured_call caught an unexpected exception outside the typed LLMClientError path and recorded it as parsing_error; this does not establish a JSON syntax defect or identify which stage failed.

What this means

  • The structured-call wrapper caught an unexpected exception outside the typed client-error path; this category alone does not establish a JSON syntax defect. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The structured-call wrapper caught an unexpected exception outside the typed client-error path; this category alone does not establish a JSON syntax defect.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained exception type and stage; if a supported response repeatedly reaches this fallback, preserve the occurrence for the client implementer.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the recorded exception message and schema name in the error details and the Server log traceback for the same time. Reproduce with the same model; if it repeats, report it with the traceback to whoever maintains SMTO or the provider integration. Raising the output token limit is not a known fix for this category.
  • Inspect the recorded exception type and structured-call stage. Have the client or provider owner repair a reproducible failure; do not assume increasing a token limit will fix this broad category.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The same structured-call boundary returns a value accepted by its output model, with any underlying defect separately identified.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
